nice_guideline_used: NICE NG203 (Chronic kidney disease: assessment and management) and NICE TA775 (SGLT2 inhibitors for CKD)

medications.dose: 2.5 mg orally once daily; titrate up to 10 mg once daily as tolerated
medications.duration: Lifelong – review annually and after each dose change
medications.purpose: RAAS blockade to reduce proteinuria and control blood pressure
medications.nice_justification: NG203 recommends ACE‑I/ARB for CKD with ACR ≥ 30 mg/mmol or hypertension; monitor creatinine & potassium after 1–2 weeks

medications.duration: Lifelong – stop if eGFR falls <20 mL/min/1.73 m²; review renal function at 4 weeks then every 3‑6 months
medications.purpose: Slow CKD progression and provide cardiovascular protection, usable even without diabetes
medications.nice_justification: TA775 recommends dapagliflozin 10 mg daily for CKD with ACR ≥ 30 mg/mmol or eGFR 20‑45 mL/min/1.73 m²

medications.dose: 20 mg orally once daily (increase to 40 mg if LDL‑C target not met)
medications.duration: Lifelong – lipid profile at 3 months then annually
medications.purpose: Cardiovascular risk reduction (CKD is a CVD‑risk equivalent)
medications.nice_justification: NG203 advises statin therapy for all CKD patients for CVD risk reduction

contraindications.reason: eGFR 20.5 mL/min/1.73 m² (<30) – risk of lactic acidosis
Accelerate CKD progression and cause fluid retention in stage 4 CKD
Increased risk of hyperkalaemia and acute kidney injury; guideline forbids dual RAAS blockade
High risk of contrast‑induced nephropathy when eGFR < 30

assumptions_warnings: Blood pressure reading not available – assume target <130/80 mmHg not yet achieved; consider adding amlodipine if BP remains uncontrolled after ACE‑I titration.
Baseline serum potassium, sodium, and liver function tests not recorded – must be obtained before starting ramipril and atorvastatin and monitored after dose changes.
HbA1c and glycaemic control not provided – dapagliflozin will be used for renal protection; further glucose‑lowering therapy may be needed after labs.
Allergy status unknown – verify no ACE‑I, statin, or sulfonylurea allergies before prescribing.
Urine microscopy shows pyuria (29 /HPF) – treat any active urinary tract infection before initiating dapagliflozin to reduce infection risk.
No current medication list – interactions assumed none, but re‑check when new drugs are added.
treatment_summary: Start ramipril 2.5 mg daily (titrate to 10 mg), dapagliflozin 10 mg daily, and atorvastatin 20 mg daily to address proteinuric CKD stage 4, diabetes‑related renal decline, and high cardiovascular risk, in line with NICE NG203 and TA775. Monitor renal function, electrolytes, and liver enzymes; avoid metformin, chronic NSAIDs, and dual ACE‑I/ARB therapy. Provide lifestyle advice and arrange follow‑up labs in 2 weeks, then every 3‑6 months.
